name: AI Collections Assistant
value_proposition: A weekly collections queue that you review yourself: it sets aside disputed, promised, and below-minimum invoices with a visible reason, matches each draft's tone to how overdue the invoice is, and carries a weekly outcome log forward so the same invoice is not chased twice by mistake.
persona: The owner or office manager of a professional-services firm, agency, B2B trades business, or clinic that bills on net-15 or net-30 terms. Overdue invoices hold a meaningful amount of earned cash, and the owner personally dislikes chasing payment.
problem: Cash is earned but not collected. Follow-up is irregular and in no particular order. Messages sometimes go out about the wrong invoice, such as one that is disputed or already has a promised payment date, which can damage the customer relationship.
workflow: 1. The person exports the overdue-invoice aging report as CSV from QuickBooks, Xero, or their invoicing tool. It needs these columns: invoice, customer, amount, due_date, days_overdue, status, notes, plus the export's as-of date. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to include. Remove contact emails, phone numbers, and any other columns the workflow does not need.
2. The person opens last week's outcome log, if one exists, and makes sure every outcome from last week is recorded (paid, promised with a date, disputed, payment plan, or no reply).

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant, such as chat history, training use, and file retention, before uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to upload the export or paste the rows as text, or not use AI for this data at all.
4. The person pastes the Weekly Collections Queue Prompt and their personal rules from the Skip Rules and Tone Ladder Worksheet, then attaches the export and the outcome log.

5. AI applies the skip rules before anything else. It sets aside disputed invoices, credit memos, invoices on a payment plan, invoices whose promised payment date has not passed as of the export date, and invoices below the owner's minimum. Every skipped invoice is listed with its reason.

6. AI ranks the remaining invoices by age band, oldest band first, then by amount, largest first. When payment history is provided, the customer's usual payment pattern is used only as a tie-breaker and is labelled AI INTERPRETATION.

7. AI assigns a tone from the owner-approved ladder (default: friendly at 1-14 days, firm at 15-44 days, phone call recommended at 45+ days). It writes each draft or call note using only the invoice number, amount, and due date from the export. Drafts never threaten legal action and never mention fees that the export does not contain.

8. The person checks every draft against its export row with the Draft Review Checklist. PERSON DECIDES: for each invoice, whether to send, edit, call, hold, or skip. The person picks the recipient from their own contacts and sends from their own email client. Nothing is sent automatically.

9. The person records each outcome in the outcome log. PERSON DECIDES: whether a dispute is resolved and the invoice can be chased again. Next week's run reads the log, so promised dates are respected and disputes stay skipped until the person changes them.
before: The owner scrolls the aging report occasionally and writes a few awkward emails to whichever customers come to mind. Sometimes they chase an invoice that is already disputed or has a promised payment date. There is no record of what was promised last week.
after: Each week the owner reviews a queue that puts the oldest and largest invoices without disputes or promises first. Every skipped invoice is shown with its reason, the tone matches the invoice's age, and every number in a draft is checked against the export row before the owner sends it themselves. An outcome log carries promises and disputes into the next week's run.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/ai-collections-assistant using a fictional aging report of 8 invented invoices dated as of 2026-06-08, with a fictional owner minimum of $150 and the default tone ladder. It shows the skip rules setting aside 2 invoices with reasons, a ranked queue of 6 with tones assigned by age band, a number check of one draft against its export row, an outcome log feeding a mock next-week run where a promised invoice is still skipped, and an ending that states the person sends every message. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The export: show the fictional aging report as a table of 8 rows (INV-3307, INV-3312, INV-3290, INV-3315, INV-3281, INV-3309, INV-3318, INV-3301) with the as-of date 2026-06-08, the fictional minimum of $150, and the tone ladder (friendly 1-14 days, firm 15-44 days, phone call recommended 45+ days).

Step 2 of 6 - Skip rules first: list the five skip rules, then show 2 invoices set aside with reasons. INV-3312 is skipped because payment was promised for 2026-06-12; re-check after that date. INV-3290 is skipped because it is disputed and needs your decision.

Step 3 of 6 - The ranked queue: show 6 invoices in order (INV-3301, INV-3281, INV-3307, INV-3309, INV-3315, INV-3318), each with days overdue, a CONFIRMED status line, and an assigned tone. Show AI INTERPRETATION: none, because no payment history was provided.

Step 4 of 6 - Check the draft: open the INV-3307 draft. A 'Check numbers against the export row' button shows three rows (invoice number INV-3307, amount $3,900 vs 3900, due date May 1 vs 2026-05-01), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - Outcome log and next week: show the fictional outcome log for the week of 2026-06-08, then a mock run as of 2026-06-15. INV-3307 is skipped because the promised date 2026-06-19 has not passed. INV-3290 is still skipped because it is disputed. INV-3315 and INV-3312 are gone because they were paid. The queue is INV-3301, INV-3281, INV-3309, INV-3318.

Step 6 of 6 - You send it: state 'You send it. Nothing is sent automatically.' and explain that the person picks the recipient, edits, and sends from their own email, or makes the call. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All invoices, customers, amounts, and dates on this page are fictional. No real business or customer data is used, and nothing is connected to an accounting system or email account.

kit_contents.title: Weekly Collections Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for the weekly run. It covers exporting the aging report from QuickBooks, Xero, or an invoicing tool with the required columns and as-of date, removing columns the workflow does not need, checking the AI tool's data settings before uploading, and setting the minimum amount and tone ladder. It also notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Weekly Collections Queue Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that applies the skip rules first, ranks by age band then amount, assigns tone from the ladder, drafts using only the invoice number, amount, and due date, and labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It forbids sending, legal threats, and invented facts.

kit_contents.title: Week-to-Week Update Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt for the following week. It reads the previous outcome log with the new export, keeps disputed invoices skipped until the person marks them resolved, skips promised invoices until the promised date has passed, and flags missed promises as CONFIRMED facts from the log.

kit_contents.title: Skip Rules and Tone Ladder Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets their minimum amount, tone band limits, and customers to always skip. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the queue prompt. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Outcome Log Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (week_of, invoice, customer, action_taken, outcome, promised_date, notes) with the allowed outcome values (paid, promised, disputed, payment plan, no reply) and fictional example rows. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Draft Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before sending each draft. It confirms that the invoice number, amount, and due date match the export row, that the recipient was chosen by the person, that the invoice is not disputed, promised, or on a payment plan, that the tone matches the age band, and that there are no legal threats or invented facts.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Aging Report
kit_contents.purpose: The same 8-row fictional CSV used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real customer data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling customer financial data in AI tools: review data settings, remove unneeded columns, do not paste bank or card details, and remember that plan and admin settings differ. It also covers tone limits (no legal threats, no fees not in the export) and the rule that nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.

decision_rules: Compute days overdue from the export's as-of date, not today's date. If the export has no as-of date, ask the person for it before building the queue.
Apply all skip rules before ranking or drafting. Skipped invoices are never ranked or drafted.

Skip any invoice whose status or latest outcome-log entry is disputed. Show the reason 'disputed; needs your decision'. It stays skipped in later weeks until the person changes the log entry to resolved.
Skip credit memos and any row with a zero or negative amount. Show the reason 'credit memo or non-positive amount'.
Skip any invoice marked as on a payment plan in the export or the outcome log. Show the reason 'on a payment plan'.

Skip any invoice with a promised payment date on or after the as-of date. Show the reason 'payment promised for <date>; re-check after that date'. If the promised date is before the as-of date and the invoice is still open, return it to the queue with the CONFIRMED note 'promise of <date> missed'.
Skip any invoice whose amount is below the owner's minimum. Show the reason 'below your minimum of $<minimum>'.
If a row is missing its invoice number, amount, or due date, or the same invoice number appears twice, do not draft it. List it under 'needs your check'.

Rank the remaining invoices by age band (45+ days, then 15-44, then 1-14 or the owner's custom bands), then by amount, largest first, then by earlier due date. Use the customer's usual payment pattern only as a tie-breaker, only when payment history is provided, and label it AI INTERPRETATION.
Assign tone strictly from the owner-approved ladder (default: friendly 1-14 days, firm 15-44 days, phone call recommended 45+ days). Invoices at 45+ days get a call note instead of an email draft.
Drafts and call notes may state only the invoice number, amount, and due date from the export row. Do not invent payment history, contact names, late fees, interest, or deadlines.
Never threaten legal action, collections agencies, credit reporting, or service suspension in any draft.
If a customer has more than one invoice in the queue, list them together and recommend one combined message. The person decides whether to combine them.
human_ai_boundary: AI applies skip rules and lists every skipped invoice with its reason. The person decides whether to resolve a dispute, accept a promise, or override a skip.
AI ranks the queue by the stated rules. The person decides which invoices to chase this week and in what order.
AI assigns a tone from the ladder the owner approved. The person sets the ladder and can change the tone of any individual draft.
AI drafts emails and call notes using only export fields. The person checks every number against the export row, edits the wording, and approves it.
AI never chooses or sees the recipient address. The person addresses and sends every message from their own email client or makes the call themselves.
AI reads the outcome log. Only the person records outcomes, and the log reflects what the person entered, not what AI assumed.

AI labels CONFIRMED facts (from the export or log), AI INTERPRETATION (for example, a payment-pattern tie-breaker), and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, refunded, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person sends each message from their own email.
Atlas does not connect to QuickBooks, Xero, an invoicing tool, or email. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before uploading an export to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove columns the workflow does not need, such as emails and phone numbers.
The kit tells the person not to paste bank account numbers, card numbers, or tax IDs into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.
Drafts never threaten legal action, collections agencies, credit reporting, or service suspension, and never mention fees or interest that the export does not contain.
Disputed and promised invoices are skipped with a visible reason so they are not chased by mistake.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, recovery rates, time savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout.
required_data_tools: Accounts-receivable aging report exported as CSV from QuickBooks, Xero, or an invoicing tool, with invoice, customer, amount, due date, days overdue, status, notes, and an as-of date
Outcome log spreadsheet, started from the kit's Outcome Log Template
Optional customer payment history, used only as a tie-breaker
The owner's own email client and phone for sending and calling
A file-capable AI assistant such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/ai-collections-assistant and the Premium kit at /blueprints/ai-collections-assistant/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or My Blueprints.

The Premium kit requires sign-in with requireUser from src/lib/auth.ts, the same pattern as app/blueprints/daily-inbox-briefing/starter-kit/page.tsx. It is labelled "Premium · Private preview". It shows no price, checkout, or claim that it can be bought today.
All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
